record_identity.title: Concurrent ChatGPT, Claude and Grok service outages on 3 September 2026

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 3 September 2026 concurrent ChatGPT, Claude and Grok service outages
incident_identity.date_basis: OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI each reported service-availability incidents on 3 September 2026. OpenAI reported elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex; Anthropic reported a partial Claude outage affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API; xAI reported a Grok models outage across multiple surfaces. The incidents overlapped in time, but the reviewed evidence does not establish a single shared technical cause.

summary: On 3 September 2026, ChatGPT/Codex, Claude and Grok experienced overlapping service-availability incidents. OpenAI reported elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex and separately attributed its disruption to a routing error. Anthropic reported a partial Claude outage caused by an infrastructure issue, affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API. xAI reported a Grok models outage across multiple surfaces and later attributed its disruption to an outage at its Memphis compute centre. The temporal overlap is material ecosystem evidence, but no reviewed source establishes that the three providers shared one technical cause.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's public status record establishes degraded performance affecting ChatGPT and Codex on 3 September 2026, and an OpenAI spokesperson separately attributed its disruption to a routing error. Anthropic confirmed a roughly three-hour partial Claude outage affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API and attributed its occurrence to an infrastructure issue. xAI's own status pages record a Grok models outage beginning at 13:30 UTC across multiple service surfaces, with traffic restored roughly three and a half hours later; xAI later stated that the disruption followed an outage at its Memphis compute centre. Independent reporting documents that the three provider incidents overlapped in time. Cloudflare and the major public-cloud status pages did not report a relevant shared disruption, and no reviewed evidence establishes one common technical cause across OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Three major frontier-AI service providers experienced overlapping availability failures on the same day. The available evidence gives different provider-specific explanations: OpenAI attributed its disruption to a routing error, Anthropic to an infrastructure issue, and xAI to an outage at its Memphis compute centre. The coincidence is relevant to resilience, concentration, dependency and correlated-failure analysis, but it does not establish a shared cloud, network, control-plane or infrastructure dependency.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence demonstrates that simultaneous or near-simultaneous loss of access to multiple frontier AI providers can create ecosystem-level resilience risk even where the individual provider failures have different or unresolved causes. It is relevant to organisational fallback design, provider concentration, correlated-outage monitoring and sovereign assurance, while preserving the distinction between temporal correlation and proven common causation.
assessment_boundaries: The reviewed evidence establishes overlapping availability incidents at OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI but does not establish that they shared one technical cause.
OpenAI attributed its disruption to a routing error; Anthropic described an infrastructure issue; xAI later attributed its disruption to an outage at its Memphis compute centre.
Cloudflare and the major public-cloud status pages did not report a relevant shared disruption during the reviewed window.
Affected-user counts, aggregate transaction loss and downstream organisational impacts across the three providers are not publicly quantified.
No data-loss, confidentiality, integrity, safety or persistent downstream harm common to all three providers is established.

dimensions.assessment_basis: The preserved sources establish the bounded consequence described in the Incident summary: On 3 September 2026, ChatGPT/Codex, Claude and Grok experienced overlapping service-availability incidents. OpenAI reported elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex and separately attributed its disruption to a routing error. Anthropic reported a partial Claude outage caused by an infrastructure issue, affecting Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API. xAI reported a Grok models outage across multiple surfaces and later attributed its disruption to an outage at its Memphis compute centre.
